\begin{tablenotes}\footnotesize
\item The floor $|\operatorname{cor}(S,x)|\ge c$ is a cut on the SEARCH set, not evidence about $\delta_0$.
After the FWL residualisation $x$ and $r$ are orthogonal, so
$\operatorname{cor}(S,x)=(1+\delta^2)^{-1/2}$ on the working scale and the floor admits exactly
$\delta\le\sqrt{c^{-2}-1}$ --- a deterministic function of $c$ that would look the same on
uninformative data.
\item The identification-robust set $\mathcal S$ itself does NOT move with $c$: the $\mathcal S$-set share of $\mathcal D$ is identical in every row, as \texttt{siv\_identification\_set()} never sees the floor.
The last column is the share of $\mathcal S$ the floor retains, so it is a denominator of $\mathcal S$,
not of $\mathcal D$; a value of 100\% means no part of $\mathcal S$ was trimmed, not that
$\mathcal S$ covers $\mathcal D$.
\item Raising $c$ to reach a single root removes a competing root; it does not identify one.
\end{tablenotes}
